question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations given by

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+y=0 \\ kx+2y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the system has a unique zero solution, which of the following statements are true?

I. The lines $x+y=0$ and $kx+2y=0$ don't intersect

II. $k=2$

III. The coefficient matrix is invertible
question.worked_solution:
Recall that given $A=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}]$, then according to the invertible matrix theorem the following statements are equivalent:    

1\. $A$ is invertible.

2\. The system $Ax=b$ has exactly one solution for any $2\times 1$ column vector $b.$

3\. The system $Ax=0$ has the unique zero solution.

4\. The lines ${a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1}$ and ${a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2}$ intersect at exactly one point.

5\. $det(A)\ne 0.$

Also, we are told that the third part of the invertible matrix theorem is true. So, all the other parts of the theorem are true too. Therefore, according to the theorem:

- Statement I is false by the fourth part of the invertible matrix theorem.

- Statement II is false. If $k=2$ then

$$
det[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ \text{ }k & 2\end{aligned}]=det[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ \text{ }2 & 2\end{aligned}]=1\cdot 2-1\cdot 2=0,
$$

but  according to the fifth part of the invertible matrix theorem, the determinant cannot be $0.$

- Statement III is true by the first part of the invertible matrix theorem.

Therefore, only statement III is true.
